title: Your private Evermind, on your machine — with local models, connectors and approvals from your phone
description: Synapse now runs local models sized to your computer and serves them to Claude Code and your scripts, hosts MCP connectors the Brain can use, lets you approve an agent's step from your phone, and gives you a private model to start from. Everything it learns stays on your machine unless you publish it.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Spawn — build Roblox games by talking
description: Spawn is a desktop builder for Roblox creators 13 and up. Describe the game, and it builds the parts, the Luau and the UI inside Roblox Studio. It connects by itself, every build is one undo step, failed builds are free, and safety rules for young creators are built in.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Describe a story, get a movie — video on the canvas
description: The canvas now turns a sentence into a real video clip, and a story into a planned, rendered and edited short movie. Studio can put generated clips straight into the apps it builds.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Studio makes the images your app needs
description: Builderforce Studio now generates the hero art, illustrations and product shots in the apps it builds, stores them in your workspace, and writes permanent links into the code, so a first draft looks like the real thing.
author: Sean Hogg

title: The canvas knows where you are — and shows you the way to the next phase
description: Measure used to open on a board with nothing live. Now every canvas reads its own board, opens on the next phase you have not done, and turns a phase you are not ready for into the shortest path there. Two new places come with it, Operate for what is running and Launch for putting it in front of people.
author: Sean Hogg

title: The App on your canvas is now a real project
description: Press App on any canvas and you get the full Studio workspace in place, with real files, a runtime that can run a server, a terminal, a database and publishing. No account is needed to start, and "Keep your work" carries the app into one.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Builderforce Studio — describe an app, watch it run, keep every version
description: studio.builderforce.ai turns a prompt into a running app in one window. Every agent turn becomes a version you can restore, the app's data has its own Database view, and Node, Vue and Svelte projects run right in your browser.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Put the model you trained on Hugging Face, from the page you trained it on
description: A trained Evermind used to leave Builderforce as a zip on your laptop, and getting it onto the Hugging Face Hub was a separate job with separate tools. Now you pick a repository, paste your own token, and the full model repo lands on the Hub from the export panel.
author: Sean Hogg

title: A private brain on your desktop that hands the work to your agents
description: Synapse now signs in to Builderforce and brings your chats to the desktop. Ask the Brain and it answers with what your private Evermind has learned on your machine; assign an agent and address it with @, and it does the work with its own tools. A live brain in the sidebar shows what you know, what you have done, and what it is learning right now.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Teach it once, and it does it again
description: Synapse can now learn a task by watching you do it once in any Windows program, turn it into a skill that asks for new values each time, run it on request or on a schedule, stop for your OK before anything irreversible — and teach your private Evermind the procedure. Opt-in, local, and forgettable.
author: Sean Hogg

title: One local index for every AI tool on your machine
description: Synapse indexes your repositories on your own computer — every definition, a map ranked by what the code depends on, search by meaning — and hands that context to the VS Code agent, Claude Code and Cursor alike. Memories that name code you have since deleted are flagged instead of obeyed. Nothing is uploaded.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Write the idea down before it's gone — and know which ones you've actually tested
description: Every canvas now has an Ideas scratchpad. Capture an idea in a sentence, track it from first thought to validated, and plan the customer interview that tests it — on the same board where it becomes real.
author: Sean Hogg

title: List your startup, meet investors, and watch your runway on the same board
description: A company could be built, run and measured here and still not be found. Now a founder lists the company in the Marketplace, investors express interest straight into the workspace, and Finance opens on the one number every founder acts on — with its source named.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Choose who answers, not just who you ask
description: A chat with teammates and agents asks two things on every turn — who you are talking to, and who is answering. The editor could only set the first. Now “Acting as” is in VS Code too, so you can run the Brain as a persona or as one of your agents, and a question put to a whole board shows everyone it went to.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Design the room you meet in — then walk it
description: The room on your board used to be one room. Now it is a boardroom, an office kitchen or an open floor of desks — or a room you lay out piece by piece, walk through like a game, sell in the marketplace, and play your Roblox place inside.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Sign it off, read the numbers, plug in your own tools — inside the room
description: The canvas could already tell you a change needed a signature, define every metric once, and register a third-party widget. It just had nowhere to do any of the three. The room now has an approval desk, a live metrics board and stands for third-party widgets.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Delegate the search, not the decision
description: An agent that spends twenty turns finding one file has no room left to think about it. Sub-agents send that search to a second agent with its own context and bring back one paragraph — on every surface an agent runs on, and now they can make the change too.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Every account gets a sales programme
description: The pipeline, the campaigns, the weekly numbers, the payouts and the referral link were already built — and only Builderforce's own associates could open them. Now every account owns one, and Reach is where it lives.
author: Sean Hogg

title: One canvas, running inside another
description: Offboarding an employee is a flow. So is promoting one — and it contains the first. Until now every canvas was a closed system and the shared part had to be redrawn in each. A canvas can now be placed on another canvas as a single step, with the parameters it accepts read off the board itself.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Send someone the link — and let them join without an account
description: Sharing a canvas used to get worse the moment you signed up. Any saved board can now produce a link that grants view, comment or edit access, and whoever opens it can join by typing a name — no signup, no password, a real collaborator.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Stand up inside your board
description: A standup is about the work in front of you, and until now it happened somewhere else. The room surface puts your team in a circle on the board itself, with the session's work on the wall behind you.
author: Sean Hogg

title: The run that teaches the next one
description: An agent that finishes verified work has just executed a procedure that works — and it used to vanish into a transcript. Agents now propose what they learned as a skill, your team approves it, and every later run follows it.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Twenty-four things landed on your board. Here is where to start.
description: A generated canvas is the product working and, for the person who asked one question, a wall. The walkthrough groups what was made, orders it by what feeds what, and takes you round it one stop at a time.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Import a quarter of records at once — and see the board lenses move
description: The People, R&D, Quality and AI lenses on the Insights board always read from real tables, and for the datasets with no connector the only way in was one row at a time. Import now takes a file, maps its columns onto the server's own registry, checks every row before writing, and posts in batches you can watch land.
author: Sean Hogg

title: See what the agent changed — before you commit it
description: An agent in your editor can edit your working tree, and the conversation used to be the only record that it had. The VS Code extension now carries a Changes section with a count badge and a pending-changes bar in the chat itself, so unreviewed edits announce themselves and every one is a click from its real diff.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Ship from the editor — commit, branch, pull request
description: The agent in your editor can now finish the job it started. git_commit, git_push and open_pull_request give it a ticket branch and a review, not a shell. Asked to push straight to main, it offers a pull request instead — and pushing the base branch is a separate, declared act your approval gate prompts for.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Grade the proof — how a kill condition turns a launch into a decision
description: Most teams record what they built and never what they learned. A proof now carries a verdict — met, missed or abandoned — with the number that decided it, which is what turns Idea to Real from a line into a loop.
author: Sean Hogg

title: The metrics your vertical actually runs on, installed in one click
description: Every company has a finance tab. Almost none of them have the six numbers their own vertical is judged by. KPI dashboards ship as marketplace templates now — pick your sector, install, and the tiles your peers track are already on the board.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Run the app your board just built — without leaving the board
description: A canvas that writes a backend, a page and a setup note used to have nowhere to run them. The app surface assembles every code card into one working application, at real device widths, on the same board you built it on.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Build a 3D world in the browser — and walk around in it
description: Place props, move a camera and walk a scene with real physics, on the same canvas that writes your code. Games made here play, including a Roblox place decoded and walked in the browser.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Read any PDF — including the scanned ones nobody can search
description: Modern PDFs store glyph indices, not letters, which is why so many tools hand back gibberish. Here is what actually goes wrong, and what happens now when you drop a scan, a contract or a résumé on the board.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Four bands of chrome, removed — the canvas gave the screen back to the board
description: A workspace that spent a quarter of the window on controls, and what changed when the rule became: collapse hides controls, never status. With before and after.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Close the deal on the board you built it on
description: Quotes that can be accepted, sequences that stop on a reply, trials with criteria agreed up front, trust packets and mutual action plans — the commercial half of the work as objects, next to the work itself.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Fixed-price milestones, with the money held until it is delivered
description: Escrow only works when both sides can see the same balance and the same next move. Here is how milestone funding, delivery, acceptance and release work when the schedule lives beside the work.
author: Sean Hogg

title: From offer to payroll without retyping anything — and the HR system you already run
description: Two funnels used to stop next to each other: hiring ended at an accepted offer, and people started with an employee record somebody typed. Here is the handover, and the read-only connectors that stop headcount being guesswork.
author: Sean Hogg

title: The founder back office — money in, ownership, and the paperwork before all the other paperwork
description: Invoices you can issue and chase, ageing computed rather than typed, a cap table recorded as events instead of a percentage column, and the four founding documents as templates you can actually send for signature.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Fifteen career tools that compute an answer — and a salary guide that names your city
description: Score a résumé, match it to a posting, tailor it, plan a route to a target role, prepare interview questions, check your market salary. Free, no account, and every number shows its working.
author: Sean Hogg

title: The four questions an enterprise AI purchase actually turns on
description: Not "which model". Can it read our data, will it leak across tenants, what did that answer cost, and how do we know it is getting better — and what an honest answer to each looks like.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Escape Your Diagramming Tool — Visio, Lucidchart, Miro and Excalidraw, In
description: Practical migration routes out of the commercial diagramming tools, what each export format actually preserves, and how to turn a picture back into editable shapes.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Every Diagram Format the Creation Canvas Reads and Writes
description: Nine notations — Draw.io, Mermaid, PlantUML, Graphviz DOT, BPMN 2.0, Excalidraw, ArchiMate, SVG and Visio — read into one shared graph, so any diagram you have can become any diagram you need.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Idea to Real — the operating methodology behind Builderforce
description: Four stages say where you are. Three acts say what you do. This is the method Builderforce is built around, why the middle act is the one that matters, and how a kill condition turns a straight line into a loop.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Which Diagram Should You Draw? Twelve Types, With Examples
description: Flowchart, sequence, class, ER, state, C4, BPMN, mindmap, Gantt, journey, dependency graph and deployment diagram — what each one is actually for, and a working example you can paste.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Eight ways to make an idea real — and how to pick one
description: A demo video, a clickable prototype, a smoke test, a Wizard of Oz, a proof of concept, a pilot, a phone line, or the whole system running. Each answers a different question and costs a different amount. Here is the map.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Read, Prove, Build — why reading an idea should cost nothing
description: Three acts, and the first two are free on purpose. A look at what actually happens when a brief is read, why planning and building are two separate calls, and what a build really produces.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Idea · Make · Run · Measure — when a menu becomes a methodology
description: Most product navigation is an org chart. Builderforce groups every destination by where it sits in the journey instead, generates the marketing site from the same list, and lets a build script prove the two can never disagree.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Creation Canvas Guide: Build, Analyze, Collaborate, and Work in 3D
description: A practical guide to Creation Canvas functionality, including objects, Brain scope and review, file and data workflows, 2D and 3D navigation, collaboration, and export.
author: Sean Hogg

title: What’s New: An Always-On Canvas, Native Files, and Connected Tools
description: Builderforce’s latest release keeps the Creation Canvas at the center of the product, opens tools and reference pages beside your work, and adds richer files, integrations, sharing, and local-first creation.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Learn How to Build an LLM—from Data to Deployment
description: Generate a complete interactive LLM course on the Creation Canvas, work through hands-on labs and assessments, and export the training to any SCORM-compatible LMS.
author: Sean Hogg

title: AI Coding and Agent Platforms — A Criteria-First Guide
description: A practical framework for evaluating AI editors, terminal agents, hosted engineering agents, open runtimes, and connected delivery platforms without relying on stale rankings.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Builderforce.ai and Claude Code — Terminal Agent or Connected Delivery?
description: Compare terminal-centered engineering with a multi-surface creative and delivery system using current requirements.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Builderforce.ai, Cursor, and Windsurf — Canvas or AI-Native Editor?
description: A criteria-first comparison of AI-native editing and connected human-and-agent delivery.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Builderforce.ai and Devin — Compare the Operating Model
description: Compare hosted autonomous engineering and connected human-and-agent delivery without relying on stale prices or binary claims.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Builderforce.ai and GitHub Copilot — Which Workflow Are You Buying?
description: Compare editor assistance with a connected creative canvas and governed delivery using current, testable criteria.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Brain Is a Canvas Operator, Not a Chatbot Beside the Work
description: Builderforce Brain can read a scoped Creation Canvas, author supported object fields, arrange objects, create typed relationships, and propose native actions through a review-before-mutation contract.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Create Before You Sign Up: A Private Canvas That Grows With the Work
description: Start a complete Builderforce Creation Canvas on your device without an account, then sign in only when publishing, delivery, training, integrations, or live collaboration need durable workspace resources.
author: Sean Hogg

title: From Blank Canvas to Repeatable Playbook: Templates, Frames, Branches, and Checkpoints
description: Start with Builderforce Creation Canvas packs, save reusable frames, preserve named checkpoints, branch experiments, and merge objects explicitly instead of copying entire workspaces.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Design, Build, and Debug in One Spatial Workspace
description: Connect Website and WYSIWYG prototypes to code, repository context, editor selections, diagnostics, terminal output, local services, and browser previews in one Creation Session.
author: Sean Hogg

title: 48 Live Objects, One Extensible Creation Canvas
description: Inside Builderforce Creation Canvas's registry-driven architecture: 48 object kinds, ten palette groups, six semantic connection types, capability gates, safe AI context, and one contract shared by web and VS Code.
author: Sean Hogg

title: From Raw Rows to a Live Data Story on One Canvas
description: Import tabular evidence, profile it, create charts and KPIs, assemble dashboards and reports, and preserve the source relationships behind an executive data story in Builderforce Creation Canvas.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Run Visual Team Rituals With Humans and AI Agents
description: Gather staff and agents into a shared stand-up object, surface progress and blockers, and turn approved follow-ups into connected work without losing the context of the ritual.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Build, Tune, and Evaluate an Evermind Model on the Creation Canvas
description: Design an Evermind model pipeline visually, connect datasets and evaluation gates, collaborate with specialists, and deliver a governed model without leaving the Creation Canvas.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Compare Projects Visually and Build an Evidence-Backed Executive Roadmap
description: Use Builderforce Creation Canvas to compare project features, maturity, performance, and delivery evidence, then turn the result into an executive or sales roadmap.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Beyond Chat — Why Creation Needs a Canvas, Not Another Prompt Window
description: Builderforce Creation Canvas keeps the familiar AI prompt while turning workflows, websites, data, models, agents, and delivery into live objects in one durable session.
author: Sean Hogg

title: From Customer Feedback to Ten Interactive Mockups in One Session
description: A practical Creation Canvas workflow for importing customer evidence, synthesizing requested features, generating mockups, and delivering approved concepts through projects, tasks, and agents.
author: Sean Hogg

title: One Multiplayer Creation Session Across the Web and VS Code
description: See how product, design, data, and engineering collaborate with AI in the same Builderforce Creation Session across the browser and a native VS Code editor surface.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Local-First AI in the Browser, Done Properly
description: SitePoint's WebGPU guide lays out the blueprint for running LLMs entirely on-device. Here's how Builderforce implements every best practice — Chrome's Prompt API, real token streaming, Web Worker isolation, GPU-loss recovery, and a progressive-enhancement cascade — and goes beyond it with on-device WebGPU training.
author: Sean Hogg

title: From Codebase to Costed Proposal: Automated RFP & RFQ Responses
description: Builderforce.ai turns an analyzed project into a branded, costed proposal — CTO and Product-Owner agents produce cost and P&L, a phased delivery Gantt, risks, dependencies, and a capability roster matched to the ask, co-branded with the requester's palette and logo, with freshness-gated grounding so the proposal reflects the real system.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Incidents That Teach: On-Call, War Rooms, and RCAs Your Agents Learn From
description: Builderforce.ai runs incidents end-to-end — a help-desk agent, on-call rotations, timed escalation, Teams/Slack/email paging, and a per-incident war-room — then feeds the root-cause analysis to your Knowledge base and the project's Evermind, so the workforce stops repeating the same failure.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Answer Before You Pay: Memory-First Inference That Skips the LLM
description: Before a paid model call, Builderforce.ai's Brain consults the project's own memory — an exact-repeat Q&A cache plus opt-in inference on the project's Evermind — and short-circuits the LLM entirely on a confident hit. Learning fans out to every Evermind under a project, so a lesson taught once answers everywhere and the token bill falls as memory grows.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Proof of Participation: Role-Gated Delivery and the Accountability Report
description: Builderforce.ai resolves the roles a ticket requires to the humans and agents capable of each, gates sign-off behind default-deny permissions, and records an immutable Accountability Report of Who, When, Verdict, Comments, and Contribution per role — so a Product Manager is never dispatched to write code and quality is proven at the board.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Give Your AI Agents a Personality: Psychometric Personas Explained
description: Builderforce.ai lets you give an AI agent a real, measurable personality — take a short psychometric test or move sliders across frameworks like HEXACO, Enneagram, and MBTI, and the resulting trait vector compiles into prompt directives and execution parameters. A cautious reviewer and a fast prototyper genuinely behave differently, consistently, run after run.
author: Sean Hogg

title: COBIT Governance Readiness for the Agentic Enterprise
description: A plain-language guide to COBIT IT governance in the age of AI agents, including where instrumented platform workflows can contribute evidence and where controls still require review.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Multi-Party Team Chat: @-Mention a Human or an Agent in the Same Thread
description: Builderforce.ai turns AI chat into real team chat — shared threads scoped to your project, invite humans by email, invite AI agents into the room, and address any message to a specific participant. Talk to a colleague and the agent loop stays idle; @-mention an agent and it actually replies as itself, running a permission-scoped tool loop to act on the board. Works on the web and in VS Code.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Real-Time Collaboration on Builderforce: Meetings, Team Chat, and Video for Human + Agent Teams
description: Builderforce.ai is where humans and AI agents collaborate in real time — a shared Kanban board, multi-party team chat you can address to a person or an @agent, live video meetings and standups over WebRTC, shared calendars with bookable availability, and the same collaboration surface inside VS Code. One system of record, everyone (and everything) on it.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Video Meetings, Standups, and Shared Calendars on Your Agentic Board
description: Builderforce.ai adds live video and audio to your agentic workspace — WebRTC standups with cameras on the ceremony round-table, ad-hoc and direct calls, a bookable team calendar with availability windows and "Find a time", Google and Microsoft calendar sync, and one-click join from the web or VS Code. Media flows peer-to-peer and never touches the server.
author: Sean Hogg

title: The VS Code Command Center: Run Your Whole Agentic Workforce Without Leaving the Editor
description: The BuilderForce VS Code extension is a full command center for a workforce of humans and AI agents — multi-party team chat, live at-a-glance status showing which sessions are executing or need your answer, a Meetings tree you can join natively, an Evermind sidebar to inspect and train your project's self-updating model, project and task trees, and human-in-the-loop approvals. Everything, in your editor.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Hire, Assign, Track, and Pay for Work — All in One Place
description: Juggling a freelancer's task list in one app, their timesheet in another, and payment in a third is where work falls through the cracks. Here's how to run the whole loop on Builderforce.
author: Sean Hogg

title: How to Send Hiring Managers a Clean, Bias-Free Candidate Packet
description: Forwarding a pile of resumes as email attachments makes recruiters look disorganized — and invites bias. Here's how to package a shortlist into one polished, optionally anonymized packet.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Everything an Agentic Employee Can Do on BuilderForce
description: An EMP — an agentic employee — is a first-class member of your workforce, not a chatbot. Here is the full picture of what one can do: hired from a marketplace, given skills and a personality, assigned work on the same board as humans, executing in the IDE, on-prem or in the cloud, governed by approval gates, and trainable into your own model.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Migrate Without Fear: Jira, Monday, Rally, GitLab, Bitbucket and GitHub into BuilderForce
description: Every external system BuilderForce connects to, and the staged migration importer that moves you off Jira, Monday or Rally — combine projects, map item types and users, review everything, then import. Or never leave your tracker and just sync. The Brain can run the whole thing.
author: Sean Hogg

title: What's Your AI Development Maturity Level? A Free Four-Question Diagnostic
description: Most teams adopted AI coding tools and still ship at the same pace, because the tools were bolted onto an unchanged process. This free diagnostic rates where your organization actually sits across four dimensions of AI-native development — and what it takes to reach the next level.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Define a Need, the Agentic System Solves It — One Spine Under Every Agent
description: Any human defines a need in plain language, a dataset, a process chart, or a persona — and Builderforce.ai compiles it into an agent that runs in the IDE, on the desktop, or in the cloud. The compile primitive that unifies the platform is now live, end to end.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Inside Evermind: The Architecture of a Self-Updating Model
description: A technical deep-dive into Evermind — the selective state-space cortex, the write-through knowledge memory with its single-incumbent invariant, and the trainable limbic layer. The math, the proofs, and an honest account of what is measured versus what is hypothesized.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Transitioning to an Agentic Workforce: Why Evermind Changes the Math
description: A CTO/CEO guide to moving from a team of people to a team of teams. Why a frozen frontier model is the wrong foundation for an agentic workforce, how Evermind's Write-Through Cognition fixes it, and what the owned stack looks like end to end.
author: Sean Hogg

title: The AI Agent Tech Stack, Built — How Builderforce.ai Implements All Seven Layers
description: The seven-layer agent stack everyone diagrams — foundation model, orchestration, memory, RAG, tools, observability, deployment — is a shopping list of separate vendors. Builderforce.ai ships all seven as one integrated platform, and meets-or-exceeds the reference design at every layer.
author: Sean Hogg

title: The Agentic Tester: An Autonomous QA Agent That Files Its Own Bugs
description: Point the Agentic Tester at your app, give it logins, and it ranks what to test from real usage heatmaps, generates Playwright specs, drives a real authenticated browser through your hottest flows on a schedule, and files every bug it finds straight onto your board — where a fix agent picks it up.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Evermind: A Model That Learns As It Works — And Never Goes Stale
description: Frozen frontier models go out of date the moment they ship. Evermind is Builderforce.ai's self-updating model, governed by Write-Through Cognition — new knowledge is written straight through, so an update replaces what came before with no reconciliation step.
author: Sean Hogg

title: SOPs Your Agents Can Read and Your Auditor Can Trust
description: Builderforce.ai's Knowledge Management subsystem is a versioned base for SOPs, processes and docs — with read-acknowledgement audit trails for SOX, TISAX and ISO 27001, AI-assisted authoring, and real-time co-editing — so the same knowledge that proves compliance also grounds your agents.
author: Sean Hogg

title: The Planning Spine: One Dated, Cost-Bearing Hierarchy from Portfolio to Task
description: Most teams keep strategy in a slide deck, delivery in a board, and cost in a spreadsheet — and reconcile them by hand. Builderforce.ai's Planning Spine unifies portfolio, initiative, epic and task into one dated timeline where every level carries its own rolled-up cost, split CAPEX vs OPEX.
author: Sean Hogg

title: From Stack Trace to Pull Request: Error Observability with a One-Click Agent Fix
description: Builderforce.ai ingests runtime errors from your browser SDK, OpenTelemetry, Sentry, PostHog or LogRocket, groups them by fingerprint, and turns any error group into a fix task an agent picks up and ships as a pull request — closing the loop from crash to PR.
author: Sean Hogg

title: One Board, Every Tracker: Connecting Linear, Jira, Sentry and PagerDuty
description: Builderforce.ai's board connectors sync work two-ways with Linear, Jira, monday, Asana, ClickUp, ServiceNow, Freshservice, Sentry and PagerDuty — so your agent workforce can act on tickets and incidents wherever they originate, without forcing a migration.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Earn Verifiable Certificates and Actually Level Up — Not Just Collect PDFs
description: Most online courses hand you a PDF nobody can verify. Builderforce Learning gives you tamper-proof certificates, a structured path to a real goal, and momentum that keeps you going.
author: Sean Hogg

title: The System of Record for Agentic Work
description: In the agentic era, half your workforce is software — and for the first time, every unit of work is fully instrumented. Builderforce.ai turns that into one system of record where work is costed and attributed from idea to ship to learn.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Every Role Gets Its Operating Picture
description: When every unit of work is instrumented and costed, the CEO, CTO, CFO, PMO and CISO can all work from the same source of truth. Here is what each role gets from one instrumented system — and how role-based access keeps it appropriate.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Autonomous Swimlane Execution — Turn Your Kanban Board Into a Self-Driving Workforce
description: Assign an AI agent to a Kanban swimlane and the board runs itself — tickets dispatch automatically, work advances lane to lane, and execution stops only at the approval gates you choose. Here's how self-driving delivery works on Builderforce.ai.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Cut Your LLM Token Bill With a Cross-Surface Semantic Cache
description: The single biggest cost lever in an AI platform is never paying twice for the same answer. Builderforce.ai's two-tier semantic cache reuses a prior response when a new prompt means the same thing — across your browser, your agents, and the gateway.
author: Sean Hogg

title: How to Build a Career Roadmap with AI: Targets, Gaps, and a 90-Day Plan
description: Turn a vague ambition into a dated plan. This guide shows how to pick a realistic target role, run an AI gap analysis across the eight signals recruiters actually read, and convert the gaps into a 30/60/90/180-day roadmap with Career 360.
author: Sean Hogg

title: Stop Emailing References as an Afterthought — Turn Them Into a Job-Winning Asset
description: Most candidates treat references as a formality. Here's how to collect, verify, and showcase references that quietly close the deal — with full control over what stays private.
author: Sean Hogg

title: How to Sync One Master Resume to LinkedIn, Indeed, and Every Other Job Board
description: Keep one master resume and push it everywhere without copy-paste drift. This guide shows how Profile Sync generates paste-ready blocks for nine vendors and uses the Chrome extension for safe two-way sync with LinkedIn, Indeed, and more.
author: Sean Hogg

title: How to Extract Every Skill from a Job Description or Resume with AI
description: Stop reading job descriptions line by line. This guide shows how to pull every skill from any job posting or resume — grouped, deduplicated, and synonym-aware — and turn it into a skills-gap comparison with the AI Skill Extractor.
author: Sean Hogg

title: How to Ask for a Reference (and Share It So It Counts)
